analysis:
Only CHANGELOG.md is supplied, and it is documentation of the v0.10.7 candidate. I examined head lines 228-623. Lines up to 410 are new; the v0.10.6 section from 411 is largely a pre-existing shift. I could not verify source behaviour, so I treated the described controls as unverified claims.

Raised finding: sandbox setup runs the downloaded installer with `--plan` before confirmation (lines 395-409), which affects TB-013/T-061. The T-061 verbatim text was not supplied, so the exact prior contract is unverified.

Other items, no finding:
- Enabled-model filter (257-261): the provider refuses `load_model`/`prefetch_model` for models outside the filter and stops auto-adopting new builds. This is a hardening; it reduces A-004/T-027-style substitution.
- `darkbloom update --rollback` (271-277): it requires hash and signature checks, refuses when any check fails, and quarantines the rolled-back release. It interacts with T-043 (watchdog swap authority) and with downgrade and qualification generations (A-017/T-054). Whether a rolled-back, possibly revoked build is blocked from App Attest serving by coordinator-side revocation is not verifiable here.
- Status App Attest lease (267-269): status now reports authorization until the lease expires, while `unenroll` keeps the 10 s renewal requirement. This is cosmetic for T-053/T-057.
- Qwen TP prefix reuse (367-372): the SSD records are `balanced` and the existing T-041 same-account TTFT oracle is unchanged in kind, but the reuse depth and the pair-level SSD tier extend its reach. Confirm the T-041 affected files cover the cluster prefix records.
- Qwen TP folded-control wire (279-300): the load agreement binds the new wire, so a build mismatch fails closed.
- Cluster local API (554, in the retained v0.10.6 section): it binds to all interfaces by default with an API key. This is pre-existing and not new.
- Rollout notes (platform trust settings) are out of scope for this repo.

No source files were in this batch; the next pass should check the installer-plan code path and rollback code if they are included elsewhere.

findings.detail: The changelog says `darkbloom sandbox setup` now downloads install.sh before the confirmation question and runs it with `--plan`, relying on the installer to "verify the release and size this Mac without installing anything". On an already set-up Mac it runs the plan again on every `setup` call (line 405). If the installer is tampered with (misissued certificate or compromised sandbox service), it now executes as the Mac owner without any consent. The "Nothing is installed" guarantee comes from the script's own behaviour, which a tampered script does not honour. Earlier, the script plausibly ran only after `y`, so this widens TB-013/T-061 exposure. Fix: verify the installer's signature or pinned hash before the first execution, or render the plan without running remote code. Update T-061 to cover pre-consent execution.
findings.title: Sandbox setup now executes the downloaded installer (--plan) before the user confirms
